headline: Dollar Tree beat with 3.5% comps on bigger tickets despite lower traffic and raised its EPS outlook; shares jumped.

metrics.comp_label: Dollar Tree comparable store net sales (continuing ops)

guidance_note: FY26 adj. EPS raised to $6.70-7.10 (from $6.50-6.90); sales $20.5-20.7bn and comps 3-4% unchanged; Q2 comps 2.5-3.5%.
key_messages: Discretionary comps +3.9% outpaced consumables +3.2%; toys and personal care strong.
Gross margin +120 bps on mark-on, lower freight and shrink, partly offset by higher tariff costs and markdowns.
Adjusted EPS $1.74, up 38%; ~630 stores added to multi-price format, ~5,900 total.
Management called the environment dynamic, especially for lower-income households facing higher fuel costs.

consumer.income_split: Lower-income households pressured by higher fuel costs and macro uncertainty.
consumer.big_ticket: Discretionary comps (+3.9%) held up, led by toys and personal care.
consumer.pricing: Higher tariff costs partly offset margin gains; lower tariffs for part of the year and fuel costs factored into raised guidance.

macro_read: Higher tickets and multi-price items carried comps while traffic fell, with fuel costs straining lower-income households.
